rule YARA_CobaltStrike_Generic_Fixed {
    meta:
        description = "Detects Cobalt Strike beacons with reduced false positives"
        author = "SOC_Team"

        not pe.cert_is_valid() and 
        $c2_mutex
}

rule YARA_CobaltStrike_Generic {
    meta:
        description = "Detects generic Cobalt Strike beacon patterns in memory or files"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1071.001"
        false_positives = "Packed .NET assemblies, legitimate update modules"
        severity = 3

    strings:
        $beacon_config = { 2E 72 63 64 2E 64 61 74 } // '.rcd.dat' - common beacon config artifact
        $http_get = "GET / HTTP/1.1" wide ascii
        $user_agent = /Mozilla\/5\.0.*Windows NT/ wide ascii
        $xor_key = { 00 00 00 00 } // Common XOR obfuscation

    condition:
        all of ($beacon*) and #http_get > 1 and $user_agent and (uint16(0) == 0x5A4D or filename matches /(?i)\\\\Temp\\\\.*\.dll$/)
}

// IMPROVEMENT: Add exclusion for known-good Microsoft signed binaries
// Exclude if valid Authenticode signature from Microsoft Corporation
import "pe"

condition:
    not (pe.imphash() and pe.number_of_signatures > 0 and pe.signatures[0].issuer contains "Microsoft Corporation") and 
    all of ($beacon*) and #http_get > 1 and $user_agent and (uint16(0) == 0x5A4D or filename matches /(?i)\\\\Temp\\\\.*\.dll$/)

arguments.summary: A spear-phishing campaign led to a Cobalt Strike beacon execution on a high-criticality finance workstation (WS-FIN-042). The initial compromise occurred via an encoded PowerShell command launched from Outlook, which executed a malicious DLL from the user's Temp directory. The malware established C2 communication over HTTPS to a known-malicious IP (198.51.100.23). Although the sandbox analysis initially classified the payload as low-risk, SIEM and EDR data revealed extensive post-exploitation activity, including lateral movement via SMB, failed Kerberos authentication attempts, and suspicious rundll32 execution. The host file was modified, indicating potential DNS tunneling or redirection. Notably, the sandbox failed to detect critical behaviors such as LSASS memory dumping, WMI-based remote execution, and volume shadow copy deletion due to analysis environment limitations.

arguments.summary: A post-exploitation incident was identified originating from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), attributed to user CORP\jsmith. The attack began with a phishing email triggering an encoded PowerShell command from Outlook, leading to the execution of a malicious DLL via rundll32.exe. The payload established a Cobalt Strike beacon to C2 server 198.51.100.23:443. Although initial sandbox analysis underestimated the threat, SIEM and EDR data revealed extensive post-compromise activity including lateral movement via SMB, failed Kerberos TGT requests, and suspicious DNS queries. The sample hash e9f0a1b2... was previously observed in a network scan from a different host, indicating potential reconnaissance. Critical detection gaps were identified in lateral movement and credential access detection.

timeline.description: Initial network scan from external IP 192.168.1.100 to WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15) detected and blocked. Sample hash e9f0a1b2... observed in traffic.
User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook on WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42).
Encoded PowerShell executed from Outlook (T1566.001).
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned DLL from Temp directory (T1218.011).
IDS alerted on Cobalt Strike beacon C2 traffic to 198.51.100.23:443 (T1071.001).
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042 to domain controller (potential credential brute-force attempt).
SMB access from WS-FIN-042 to file server 10.0.5.50 (lateral movement, T1021.002).
Post-exploitation alert triggered on WS-FIN-042. Incident response initiated.
